Contributing to theoryforge

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution. Issues and pull requests are both welcome, whether they fix a bug, improve the documentation or add a feature.

theoryforge ships as twin packages, R and Python, from this one repository. The R package lives in r/theoryforge/ and the Python package in python/. The two are pinned to a shared specification (API_SPEC.md) so that they return identical verdicts and byte-identical diagram intermediate representations, so a change to behaviour usually needs to land in both, with the parity check kept green.

Reporting a problem or suggesting a feature

Please open an issue at https://github.com/pablobernabeu/theoryforge/issues. A small reproducible example helps a great deal. Never paste a secret, such as an OSF token or an OpenAlex API key, into an issue; replace it with a placeholder.

Setting up for development

Working from a clone of the repository, the R package:

# roxygen2 at the version DESCRIPTION records, which CI pins
pak::pak(c("devtools", "roxygen2@8.0.0", "testthat", "spelling"))
devtools::document("r/theoryforge")   # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE after editing roxygen
devtools::test("r/theoryforge")       # run the test suite
devtools::check("r/theoryforge")      # a full R CMD check

The Python package:

pip install -e "./python[dev,docs,render]"
cd python
pytest                  # run the test suite
ruff check . ../scripts # lint python/ and scripts/, as CI does
mypy src                # type-check
mkdocs build --strict   # build the docs

The documentation build draws the diagrams with Graphviz, so it also needs the Graphviz binaries on the PATH. Install them with your system’s package manager, for example sudo apt-get install graphviz or brew install graphviz, or from https://graphviz.org/download/.

The parity check and the browser apps’ checks run from the repository root. The parity check needs Rscript on the PATH, with the R packages pkgload, jsonlite and yaml. The app tests need only Node. The two smoke scripts run each app’s glue on the files node apps/build.mjs writes, the Python one with PyYAML and the R one with jsonlite and yaml (see apps/README.md).

python scripts/parity_check.py      # R against Python on every fixture
node apps/build.mjs                 # write the files the apps load
node --test apps/tests/*.test.mjs   # the app tests
python scripts/app_smoke.py         # each app's glue on those files
Rscript scripts/app_smoke.R

scripts/app_smoke_cases.json lists every operation the apps offer at the UI’s defaults, and once more for each other option of a select parameter, so a new operation, option or default needs a matching case. apps/tests/smoke.test.mjs fails when the two differ.

Conventions

British spelling throughout. In the R package, devtools::check() and CI run a spelling test that stops on any word found neither in the British English dictionary nor in r/theoryforge/inst/WORDLIST, and spelling::spell_check_package("r/theoryforge") lists those words. Correct a misspelling where it occurs, and add a name or a term of art to the word list. The two implementations are kept in lockstep through the shared API_SPEC.md, and scripts/parity_check.py compares their output and must stay green. Diagrams are emitted as byte-identical intermediate representations, so changes there are checked against the golden fixtures. The golden outputs, which cover every parity artefact and not only the diagrams, are written by the Python implementation. After a change that alters any output, or an edit to a file in fixtures/ or schema/, run python scripts/gen_golden.py from the repository root, with the Python package installed as above, and commit what it writes. The script also writes the copies that the packages ship, so edit the originals in fixtures/ and schema/, never the copies. Both packages ship the example theories and corpora and the files of schema/, under r/theoryforge/inst/ and python/src/theoryforge/, and the R package also ships the golden outputs. The fold table schema/fold.json is itself written by scripts/gen_fold_table.py. CI fails when any of these files is stale. theoryforge never stores credentials: an OSF deposit takes the token as an explicit argument to tf_osf_push() (R) or osf_push() (Python) and is never performed automatically, and an OpenAlex fetch reads its optional API key from the api_key argument or the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable.

Submitting a pull request

Base your work on main, keep the change focused, and add or update tests and documentation alongside the code. Continuous integration runs the R and Python suites, the apps’ tests, the golden-file check and the parity check on every push to main and on every pull request.

By contributing you agree that your contribution is licensed under the same MIT licence as the package, and that you will follow the Code of Conduct.
